findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/search.scss:31 — Advisory (confidence 75, P3): repeating `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 40%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 60%))` and its complementary percentage variants at 109 new call sites couples component styling to theme-selection policy, so maintainers retuning a shade must synchronize two literals and a one-literal edit leaves dark-theme users on the old shade; a single-parameter shared shade helper computing `100% - $lightness` removes the 109 explicit chooser expressions and secondary-percentage places to update, including common/base/search.scss:31,33,37 and desktop/header.scss:53,59; the strongest rebuttal is that explicit pairs preserve per-component artistic control and follow the existing chooser idiom, but every added pair sums to 100% and the helper preserves each component’s independent lightness parameter while eliminating that duplicated invariant.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/_topic-list.scss:115 — Defect (confidence 100, P2): `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still sets `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%);`, so a dark palette with white `$primary` renders category notification counts white instead of the secondary-derived muted color applied to sibling counts, leaving this explicitly targeted dark-theme conversion incomplete.

app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — Advisory (confidence 100, P2): `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));` changes the preexisting light-theme value from 70% to 30%, but the change supplies neither compiled light/dark palette comparisons nor rendered verification, leaving maintainers without acceptance evidence for unchanged light-theme appearance and complementary dark-theme colors before release; the strongest counterargument is that these are mechanical substitutions using an existing helper, which does not resolve the gap because this substitution actually changes the light branch and differs from the desktop counterpart.

app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — Defect (confidence 100, P2): `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));` changes the existing light-theme reply-author color from 30% to 70% lightness, turning #4d4d4d into #b3b3b3 with a black primary and reducing readability on a white background despite the task requesting a dark-theme fix; the same unrelated light-theme changes occur at app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 (30% to 50%), app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 (70% to 30%), and app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 (20% to 50%), so preserve the original primary percentages in all four branches.

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.
